title: Match the target parabola
statement: The dashed curve is a target parabola. Move the sliders a, h and k in y = a(x-h)^2 + k until your parabola sits exactly on top of the target.
goal: Student finds a = -0.5, h = -1, k = 4 and can say what each slider does: h shifts left/right (opposite the sign seen in (x-h)), k shifts up/down, a sets direction and width.
common_misconceptions: Expecting h to move the curve in the direction of the sign shown inside the parentheses
Thinking a only changes width and not direction (missing that negative a flips it)
Matching the vertex but not the width, or matching one side only
hint_ladder: Ask which slider they think moves the curve up and down, and have them test it.
Ask them to find the target's vertex by looking at the graph and compare it to their own vertex.
Plot the target's vertex (-1, 4) as a tutor point and ask which sliders move their vertex onto it.
Ask what happens to the curve when a is negative versus positive, then what happens as |a| gets smaller.
Plot a second target point such as (1, 2) and ask which a makes their curve pass through it.
